bug_info.bug_desc: In the old code, the alert failure counters were cleared by `rst_alert_cntr_o` pulses generated in `entropy_src_main_sm` after a passing health-test window. Those pulses are derived from the delayed `ht_done_pulse_i` / `ht_fail_pulse_i` signals, so the clear pulse can coincide with a new `any_fail_pulse` from continuous tests such as repcnt/repcnts. Since the counter clear supersedes the increment in the same cycle, the failure is silently dropped and does not count toward the alert threshold. Additionally, `ht_failed_d` was unconditionally cleared when `es_enable_fo[6]` was low, which could erase a failure on the last symbol tested before disable before the main SM could consume it. The fix moves alert-counter clearing to the actual end of the health-test window, qualified by the real `ht_failed_d` status and a level-based `alert_cntr_clr_ok` signal from the main SM, and adjusts the `ht_failed_d` state update so failures are preserved while the delayed enable is still active.
bug_info.fix_hint: Replace the main SM's one-cycle `rst_alert_cntr_o` clear pulses with a level output `alert_cntr_clr_ok_o` asserted in the health-test-running/post-check states where clearing is permitted, and remove the `rst_alert_cntr_o` assertions from the passing-window transitions. In `entropy_src_core`, compute `alert_cntrs_clr` as `health_test_clr || (health_test_done_pulse && !ht_failed_d && alert_cntr_clr_ok)`, so counters are cleared only when the actual window completes without a failure. Update `ht_failed_d` so `any_fail_pulse` can still latch a failure while `es_delayed_enable` is high, and only clear `ht_failed_d` when both `es_enable_fo[6]` and `es_delayed_enable` are low, preserving a failure on the last symbol before disable.
